newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court rules against FPBank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court rules against FPBank insolvency.

text.p: The Sofia City Court said on Wednesday it had ruled against the Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) decision to seek First Private Bank (FPB) insolvency.
"The court decided to reject the BNB's insolvency claim against First Private Bank as unfounded and not supported by evidence," the court said in a statement made available to Reuters.
The BNB could appeal the decision at the Supreme Court in seven days.
The court rejected as ungrounded BNB's claim that the bank was insolvent when the BNB put it in receivership on May 17, the statement said.

"FPB was capable to meet its dues to the BNB worth 3.8 billion levs but the BNB had set insuperable obstacles by putting the bank in receivership, depriving the bank of the possibility to do so," the statement said.

The central bank placed the FPB in receivership on May 17 dismissing its management and appointing sequestrators to establish its financial state. The bank was banned from extending credits, servicing payments and dealing in government securities.
Two weeks later the central bank opened bankruptcy procedures against Bulgaria's biggest private bank.
The court said on Wednesday it was incorrect to calculate the bank's capital-to-risk assets ratio as negative before the fiscal year or at least the first half of it was over.
The fiscal year coincides with the calendar year in Bulgaria.
"Under amendments to the banking law approved this year Bulgarian banks are required to reach a positive ratio by the year 2001," the court said.
The BNB said the FPB's assets stood in May at 48.4 billion levs and liabilities of 57.7 billion levs.
The BNB said it lent the bank some $8 million in the beginning of this year as part of a stabilisation programme which failed.
The FPB has received some 60 percent of total BNB uncollateralised refinancing to local commercial banks last year, BNB figures showed.

The BNB has placed 14 or one third of Bulgaria's banks in receivership and has so far filed insolvency suits against 13 of them in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks in a bid to stabilise the shaky banking sector.
Last week the court postponed ruling on Mineralbank and Balkanbank until March.
